title.narrative: UNDP- Strengthening Electoral Processes in Uganda (SEPU)
UNDP- Strengthening Electoral Processes in Uganda (SEPU)

description.narrative:
FN:s utvecklingsprogram (UNDP) har tillsammans med andra FN-organ, som UN Women, OHCHR och UNESCO, utvecklat ett projekt för att stödja valcykeln 2020/21 i Uganda. Projektet som har namnet ”Stärka valprocesserna i Uganda (SEPU)" följer rekommendationer från en behovsinventering angående valstöd som UNDP företog i mars 2019, och som även föreslog att UNDP skulle leda utformningen av ett dylikt samarbetsprojekt. Projektet syftar till att svara mot de utmaningar som tidigare identifierats av EU:s valobservatörer, av rättsvårdande institutioner (utfallet av en HD-dom ang valen 2016) och av den nationella valkommissionen (EC), och som negativt påverkat tidigare nationella vals kvalitet och trovärdighet.
Projektets förändringsteori är att inkluderande och transparenta val är avgörande för att konsolidera de framsteg i samhällsutvecklingen som gjorts och befästa freden som utvecklingen bygger på. Vidare är tekniskt kapabla, oberoende och pålitliga samhällsinstitutioner centrala för genomförandet av trovärdiga, inkluderande och fredliga val. Eftersom val är en konfliktutlösare som kan leda till våld och även att liv förloras, är det avgörande att fredsbyggande och konfliktförebyggande ansatser genomsyrar stödarbetet.
UNDP lämnade in ett projektförslag till Sveriges ambassad och till andra utvecklingspartner för att söka stöd till projektet ”Stärka valprocesser i Uganda (SEPU)”. Det övergripande målet för projektet är att förbättra kapaciteten och trovärdigheten hos institutioner med en central roll i valprocessen, i syfte att främja trovärdiga val under 2020/21 och därefter. Detta bidrar till Ugandas vision att bli ett fredligt, säkert och välmående medelinkomstland år 2040.
Projektspecifika mål är att: 1) Stärka öppenhet och inkludering i valprocessen, 2) Förbättra den institutionella kapaciteten för valkommissionen (EC) och andra nyckelinstitutioner, 3) Förbättra fredsbyggande mekanismer.
UNDP kommer att genomföra projektet i samarbete med tre andra FN-organ, UN Women, OHCHR och UNESCO, baserat på deras komparativa fördelar och behovet av komplementaritet. UN Women kommer att leda aktiviteter som syftar till att främja ett inkluderande valdeltagande, särskilt för kvinnor, ungdomar och människor som lever med funktionsnedsättningar. OHCHR kommer att leda arbetet med att integrera mänskliga rättigheter i alla projektaktiviteter och att övervaka respekten för mänskliga rättigheter under hela valcykeln. UNESCO kommer att bidra med kapacitetsuppbyggnad och utbildning, som t.ex. medieträning avseende konfliktfrågor och jämställdhet.
Projektet inriktas på samarbete med nationella institutioner för att förbättra deras förmåga att leverera trovärdiga val. Dessa inkluderar den nationella valkommissionen i Uganda (EC), Ugandas poliskår (UPF), rättsväsendet, Kommissionen för mänskliga rättigheter (UHRC), ministeriet för informations- och kommunikationsteknik (MoICT), Ugandas medieråd, olika medier, politiska partier och ett antal civilsamhällesaktörer.
UNDP hade ursprungligen lagt fram en total budget på 10 miljoner USD, varav UNDP:s egna finansiering uppgick till cirka 600 000 USD och resterande 9,4 miljoner USD skulle finansieras av andra givare. I dagsläget (okt 2020) uppgår totala givaråtaganden till ca 7 m USD enligt följande; UNDP: 600 000 USD Sverige: 10 MSEK (cirka 1 miljon USD) Danmark: 1 miljon USD Norge: 25 MNOK (cirka 2,7 miljoner USD) Österrike: 1,5 miljoner euro (cirka 1,7 miljoner USD)
Budget för tekniskt stöd, projektpersonalen och projektledning är ca 2 520 000 USD, projektaktiviteter: ca 3 850 000 USD samt 8% GMS (General Management Support) om motsvarande ca 560 000 USD.
Eftersom UNDP inte lyckats finna finansiering för hela den planerade projektbudgeten har de varit tvungna att prioritera bland aktiviteter i den ursprungligen godkända programplanen. De 7 musd som står till förfogande idag, kommer att bidra till aktiviteter inom outcomes 1, 2 och 3 i programdokumentet.
Projektinsatserna fokuserar kring tre tematiska utfall och en fjärde som har inriktning på projektledningsaktiviteter, enligt följande; 1. Stärkt inkludering och insyn i valprocessen - 1,493,158 USD (21%) 2. Utökad institutionell kapacitet för valkommissionen och andra intressenter inom ramen för valcykeln - 920 000 USD (13 %) 3. Förstärkt dialogkapacitet och inrättande av ett Early Warning and Rapid Response (EWER) system - 854,364 USD (12%) 4. Effektiv och ändamålsenlig projektledning, partnerskapsbildning, övervakning och utvärdering – 2,097,116 USD (29%)
Projektet kommer att anta en direktimplementeringsmodalitet (DIM), vilket innebär att UNDP samordnar och hanterar alla projektupphandlingar och samordnar rapportering till givare och nationella intressenter. UNDP kommer att inrätta ett projektteam, lett av en sk Chief Technical Advisor, för att tillhandahålla teknisk och operativ expertis i hanteringen och genomförandet av projektet. Projekt-teamet lyder under och rapporterar till UNDP:s landkontor i Uganda genom dess "Rule of Law and Constitutional Democracy Team".

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), together with other UN agencies, i.e. UN Women, OHCHR and UNESCO, have developed an electoral project to support the 2020/21 electoral cycle in Uganda. The project named “Strengthening Electoral Processes in Uganda (SEPU)” followed the recommendation of the UN Electoral needs assessment mission in March 2019 for the UN to support the 2020/21 elections in Uganda and for UNDP to lead in formulating an integrated electoral assistance project. The project seeks to respond to the various challenges earlier on identified by the EU election observers mission in their 2016 report, the Judiciary (supreme court ruling on 2016 elections), and the National Electoral Commission's own identified challenges as having adversely affected the quality and credibility of past elections in Uganda.The project is based on the intervention logic that inclusive, participatory, transparent elections are critical to sustain development gains and consolidate peace as the foundations on which development thrives; also, technically capable, independent and trusted governance institutions are essential for the conduct of credible, inclusive and peaceful elections; furthermore, elections is a conflict trigger which potentially results in violence and loss of lives; peacebuilding and conflict prevention approaches are critical to ensure peaceful and violence-free elections. UNDP submitted a project proposal to the Embassy of Sweden and to other development partners for the support of “Strengthening Electoral Processes in Uganda (SEPU)” project. The overall goal of the project is to improve the capacity and credibility of key institutions with an electoral mandate to promote credible elections, in 2020/21 and beyond, that significantly contribute to Uganda’s Vision of becoming a peaceful, secure and prosperous middle-income country by 2040. The specific objectives of the project are to: 1) Strengthen transparency and inclusion in electoral process; 2) Enhance institutional capacity for the Electoral Commission (EC) and other electoral stakeholders; and3) Improve peace building mechanisms.The project is implemented by UNDP in partnership with three other UN agencies, i.e. UN Women, OHCHR and UNESCO based on their comparative advantage and the need for complementarity of efforts: UN Women will lead on activities aimed at promoting inclusive participation in elections, especially for women, youth and People Living With Disabilities ; OHCHR will lead on human rights mainstreaming across all project activities and also human rights monitoring in the country during the entire electoral cycle; while UNESCO will support media capacity building and training including media training on conflict and gender sensitivity.The project targets and collaborates with national institutions to improve their capacity to deliver credible elections. These include; Electoral Commission of Uganda (EC), Uganda Police Force, (UPF), Judiciary/Human Rights Commission, Ministry of Information and Communication Technology (MoICT)/ Media Council of Uganda/Media and other non-state actors like political parties and a select number of civil society organisations working on elections.The project interventions are centered on three thematic outcomes with the fourth focusing on project management activities as follows; 1. Strengthened inclusion and transparency of the electoral process - 1,493,158 USD (21%)2. Enhanced institutional capacity for the Electoral Commission and other electoral stakeholder - 920,000 USD (13%)3. Strengthened dialogue capacities and electoral violence Early Warning and Rapid Response (EWER) system - 854,364 USD (12%)4. Effective and efficient project management, partnership formation, monitoring and evaluation – 2,097,116 USD (29%)

title.narrative: Decision on Amendment for Strengthening Electoral Processes in Uganda

description.narrative:
Introduction
In 2018, the Government of Uganda, through the Electoral Commission formally requested electoral support from the United Nations for the 2020/2021 elections. Following this request the United Nations conducted a Needs Assessment Mission (NAM) in March 2019. Based on the NAM recommendations, an electoral support programme called "Strengthening Electoral Processes in Uganda" (SEPU) was started by UNDP.
UNDP then reached out to several donors to support the programme. The programme was jointly funded by Sweden, Norway, Austria, Denmark, Iceland, and UNDP. It was implemented by UNDP in close collaboration and partnership with UN Resident Co-ordinator ( UNRCO), UN Women, Office Of the High Commissioner for Human Right (OHCHR) and United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO).
Other electoral stakeholders who comprised of state and non-state actors, included, the Electoral Commission (EC), Judiciary of Uganda, Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (MoJCA), Ministry of Local Government (MoLG), Uganda Human Rights Commission (UHRC), Parliament of Uganda, Media Council of Uganda, Makerere University, Inter religious Council of Uganda (IRCU) Nnabagereka Development Foundation and Women Situation Room (by the Women International Peace Centre). The Electoral Commission was the most crucial actor because of its mandate to organise and conduct regular, free and fair elections.
Implementation context The programme commenced in February 2020 and was slated to end in February 2022. However, due to several disruptions that affected its implementation, it was extended until August 2023. The first disruption arose from the Covid-19 pandemic ( March 2020-January 2022). This required UNDP to make adjustments to support the electoral process during the lock down and in line with Covid-19 Standard Operating Procedures. At this point, the World Health Organisation ( WHO) joined the programme to provide support to UNDP and the Electoral Commission.
In November 2020, the programme suffered its second challenge, when it was halted by the government citing the need for the Attorney General to review the co-operation agreement between UNDP and the government. The suspension went on for over a year until March 2022, when it was eventually lifted following UNDP's negotiations. By this time, most planned activities were no longer relevant since the elections had happened in January 2021. The government advised UNDP to revise the work plan and include support the Women Council and Committee Elections (WCCE) that were yet to take place. UNDP adjusted the work plan to include support to WCCE and other electoral stakeholders including the parliament, the judiciary and media.
In September 2022, the Ebola outbreak happened and it affected activities related to peace building that required community engagement and gatherings. UNDP adopted virtual working arrangments to continue activity implementation. At about the same time, OHCHR, one of the implementing UN agencies exited the country following government directives. In May 2023, Uganda enactment of the Anti-homosexuality Act 2023. This affected implementation of activities with the parliament, the Youth Parliamentary Forum and the Inter Religious Council because of their role in enacting the law.
Overall, the SEPU programme was implemented in a complex sociopolitical context. Nonetheless, UNDP and its partners implemented the programme and delivered results. However, the complex context influenced the type and scope of results achieved. Some of the results presented below are at output level showing only partial progress towards the over all goal. Moreover, some of the results presented are directly attributable to the programme, while others, particularly at the national level reflect outcomes to which the programme contributed through the implementation of multiple and complementary activities along side other actors.
Results
Output 1: Strengthened inclusion and transparency of the electoral process.
The programme contributed to an increase in the number of eligible voters in 2021 compared to 2016. In 2021, an 18.5% increase in the proportion of eligible voters was registered with 18,103,603 registered voters compared to 15,277,198 registered voters in 2016. The programme contributed to this result through the active voter education and mobilization campaign that was conducted by the Citizen's Coalition on Electoral Democracy (CCEDU) in partnership with UNDP. UNDP also supported 2,193 radio spot messages, DJ mentions, mobile caravans, press conferences and other engagements to improve electoral information access before the elections.
The programme also contributed to an increase in women participating as candidates in elections at national and sub-national levels. In 2021, 133 (4.9%) women contested for parliamentary positions and 20 (5.7 percent) women secured direct MP seats. Twenty two (3.6%) women contested for District Chairperson positions. This is compared to 2016 when women constituted only 5.5% of candidates in all election categories i.e for President, Member of Parliament and District or City chairperson.The programme contributed to this result through supporting the national e-conference for aspiring women candidates, conducting advocacy to enhance access to media by prospective candidates and supporting capacity building on fundraising tools for an effective political campaign for women candidates.
The programme enhanced women's access to media as a campaign tool during the Covid-19 lock down thus providing them an opportunity to favourably compete in the elections. The 2021 election campaigns were conducted during the Covid-19 lock down in 2020 and media platforms became the most favoured campaign platforms. Given the challenges that women face in accessing media platforms including limited time and economic resources, the programme supported women organisations and the Equal Opportunities Commission to have a dialogue with the Electoral Commission to identify ways in which access to media could be enhanced for women candidates. Following this dialogue, the Uganda Communications Commission lifted the ban on community radios that are easily accessible and less expensive thus providing an alternative that is favourable for women. Additionally, a Electoral Commission collaborated with National Broadcasters Association to foster transparency and equitable access to airtime on media and a uniform rate cut was agreed to be used on different media hence increasing access for the vulnerable groups.
The SEPU programme contributed to electoral policy and legislative reform. The National Womens Council Act was amended to align the timing of the Women Council Elections with the national elections. Other Bills that were enacted with technical support of the programme include the Electoral Commission (Amendment) Bill 2019, the Political Parties and Organizations (Amendment) Bill 2019, the Parliamentary Elections (Amendment) Bill 2019, the Presidential Elections (Amendment) Bill 2019 and the Local Government (Amendment) Bill.
Output 2: Enhanced institutional capacity for EC and other electoral stakeholders.
The programme improved the application of Information and Communication Technologies (ICT) in enhancing access and administration of justice through establishing Video conferencing systems in six courts and six prisons in Uganda, installation of real time transcription systems for four selected courts and provision of computer equipment for the Judicial Training Institute. Additionally, the programme supported digitization of the Registry and teleconferencing of key offices within the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs (MoJCA) and its regional offices including Ee-filing equipment and zoom licenses to support uninterrupted public service delivery. It is important to mention that this result emerged from activities designed and implemented following UNDPs reprioritization of support to the justice sector after the lifting of the suspension.
The programme also enhanced the capacity of the electoral commission and other stakeholders through capacity building training and dialogues. For example an electoral symposium was organized under the programme which enabled high level exchanges on electoral best practices in the region, enhanced capacities of the Electoral Commission, and influenced preparations and delivery on the elections.
Output 3: Strengthened dialogue capacities as well as Electoral Violence Early Warning and Early Response (EWER) system
The programme contributed to conflict prevention and peace building mechanisms in the election period through the establishment of the Womens Situation Room (WSR) and deployment of election monitors in support of the WSR. 1,284 Women peace advocates were trained and deployed in 30 districts that were identified as hot spots for election violence. The peace advocates contributed to community sensitization on peaceful elections, encouraged their children not to get involved in election violence, pushed for reconciliation for some political leaders at community level which contributed to peace before, during and after elections. The WSR provided for real time reporting of electoral violence incidents through a Google app called Amani and a call centre. 1,778 calls were received at the call centre on polling day. Majority of the callers sought information on the electoral processes and election malpractices. A few reported misinformation among voters, and intimidation. The WSR functioned well until internet was shut down by the Government thus affecting relaying of and compilation of data from the field (districts) to the national WSR centre in Kampala. The WSR then resorted to using only the toll free lines to collect such data.
Output 4: Effective and efficient project management, partnership formation, and Monitoring and Evaluation.
This output was aimed at ensuring effective coordination and delivery on project milestones. The preparations for the 2021 elections including election campaigns and dialogues were conducted during the Covid-19 pandemic. The programme contributed to supporting the World Health Organisation (WHO) to conduct activities to strengthen the capacities of the national authorities to prevent Covid19 infections during the general elections polls. The purpose of the support was to implement interventions that mitigate anticipated risks to election officials, health workers and others involved in the election process.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
